notes_for_parent: V7 is the only case in the V-family that varies the ledger COLUMN COUNT; it complements V1 (clean pair), V2 (vault tamper), V4 (vault absent), V5 (source absent) and V6 (CRLF) by isolating schema tolerance: extras ignored, canonical positions authoritative, note still read.

The r2 tool passes the three matched rows by construction (its `read -r sp ss vp vs _rest` drops extras) — so V7 alone does not discriminate r2 from a correct r4 tool; the discrimination targets a STRICTER parser that rejects >6 columns (caught by rows 1/2) and a looser one that drops hash checks (caught by row 4).

Note recording is the second half of the assignment ('note recorded'): the row's note is declared per target and recoverable from column 6; the r2 tool never surfaces it, so an r4 harness that renders VERIFIED + the note satisfies the full expectation.
The r2 tool rejects `--ledger FILE` (usage error) and takes the ledger only via SOUJI_LEDGER; runner-28 invokes r4 impls with `--ledger`. V7 declares both invocation forms in expected.json 'notes'.
Do not change the five payload digest constants without rebuilding payload/ and re-running --print-hashes; the builder fails loudly on any drift.
